statement_en: For any permutation $\pi\in S_n$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ let $S(\pi)$ count the number of distinct consecutive sums, that is, sums of the shape $\sum_{u\leq i\leq v}\pi(i)$. Is it true that\[S(\pi) = o(n^2)\]for all $\pi\in S_n$?
statement_lean:
open scoped BigOperators

def consecutiveSums (n : ℕ) (p : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : Finset ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter (fun x : Fin n × Fin n => x.1 ≤ x.2)).image
    (fun x => ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc x.1 x.2, ((p k : ℕ) + 1))

theorem erdos_94295 :
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ p : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
      ((consecutiveSums n p).card : ℝ) < c * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
  sorry
